docs.title: Team Charter
docs.text: HaMaLoYa aims to provide awareness and safety for drivers who may encounter drowsiness or fatigue while behind the wheel.

docs.title: Product Mission Statement
docs.text: HaMaLoYa's mission is to improve driver safety by developing an effective solution that can respond to fatigue or drowsiness, as these situations could happen at any moment.

docs.title: Negative Comments
docs.text: Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need “ This device certainly has a good concept, but it also has too many flaws. Of course, you cannot compare it to commercial versions with their much higher price tags. Pros: It performs certain functions when properly set up. It has a relatively low price compared to other devices. Compact size. Cons: Does not work with sunglasses. Only a few functions work with regular clear glasses. No ability to adjust the volume. Too many false-positive prompts. Since it is advertised as an AI device, it would be very helpful to have an interface that allows users to customize the settings and possibly train the AI to better recognize the driver and specific behaviors. It is also essential that the device work with both regular glasses and sunglasses. On sunny days, you simply have to wear sunglasses, so this is an important limitation. Overall, the device is an interesting concept and does perform some useful functions, but it still needs significant improvements to be truly practical for everyday use ” 1.The product is affordable (explicit)  2.The product functions as intended (explicit)  3.The product is compact (explicit)  4.The product works even with sunglasses on (explicit)  5.The product functions as intended with regular clear glasses (explicit)  5.The product has adjustable volume control (explicit)  6.The product recognizes individuals behavior (latent)  7.The product is practical for everyday use (explicit)  8.The product overall concept is good and works well (latent)  9.The product is comparable to more expensive commercial versions (latent) “DMS Driver Monitoring System AI Fatigue Warning Device with Face Recognition Alerts for Eye Closing Yawning Smoking Phone Use & Distraction Works for All Vehicles. This DMS Driver Monitoring System AI Fatigue Warning Device with Face Recognition Alerts for Eye Closing Yawning Smoking Phone Use and Distraction does what it advertises in the right conditions. Setup was straightforward and it mounts easily on the dash, and it does catch eye closing and yawning with an audible alert that is loud enough to get your attention. Face recognition works consistently in daylight and it correctly flagged phone use and looking away from the road during my testing. Would’ve liked maybe better low light performance because accuracy drops at night or with glare from streetlights, and it gave a few false alerts when I was just talking or wearing sunglasses. Would recommend with reservations because the concept is solid for long drives and fleet use, and the alerts are immediate without lag. The system installs in any vehicle and does not need phone integration, which is convenient. Best for daytime highway driving where fatigue is a risk, but do not rely on it as your only safety measure. Good idea and decent execution, just expect some calibration quirks and occasional false positives.  ” 1.The product set up is straightforward (explicit)  2.The product detects yawning and reacts to keep the driver alert (explicit)  3.The product detects eyes closing and reacts to keep the driver alert (explicit)  4.The product recognizes the drivers face in daylight (explicit)  5.The product recognizes when the driver is using a phone (explicit)  6.The product works as well in low light (explicit)  7.The product can tell between talking or wearing sunglasses as a false alert (explicit)  8.The product does not need phone integration (explicit)  9.The product has little to no false positive alerts (explicit) N/A N/A

docs.title: Project Objective
docs.text: This project aims to investigate and develop smart adaptive technologies, an improved user experience, better fit, improved product design, and product customization options for the next-generation AirPods. The target is to maintain global dominance in the wireless earphone market, drive up AirPod sales to 100 million+ units sold with a 60% global market share in 2021 and expand the user base more towards the luxury, professional, and fitness segments. We believe that adding smart interactions and adaptive audio filters alone will already expand our user base by 15%. With the new generation AirPods we aim to match at least the sound quality of our main competitor, the Sony WF-1000XM3, and include Active Noise Canceling that is also featured in Mifo, House of Marley, Bose, and Amazon Echo products. We will also obtain IPX4 sweat-resistant rating equal to Bose, House of Marley, and Amazon Echo earbuds, and aim to extend our range of colors, as seen in Urbanista and Jabra’s lifestyle products.

docs.title: Stakeholders
docs.text:
• Target group High-income upper-class professionals between the age of 20 and 45. Their personalities are determined and ambitious. The main benefits sought are recreation and self-expression.
  • Target purchaser Target group profile with special attention to Full Nest I and Full Nest II mothers.
  • Customer service Prefers easy-to-repair, recyclable product, and easy-to-fix complaints to fit with Apple’s intuitive user experience.
  • Marketing & Sales division Looks for unique selling points around the Apple Aspirer-Explorer lifestyle and user experience.
  • Retailers Prefer products that can withstand a wide range of storage conditions including variations in temperature, vibration, humidity, and atmospheric pressure, and have a strong and compact, theft, and vandalism-proof packaging.

docs.title: User Story #1: Jenna
docs.text:
Jenna is a 33-year-old executive who regularly visits a bar for lunch to blow off some steam. The bar is often loud with people, but it is paramount that she can hold business conversations over the phone there. Then again, she does not want to miss out on the atmosphere and be able to hear the waiters as well. Her new Apple wireless earphones allow her to switch instantly between a mode where she can fully focus on the phone conversation and a mode where the phone call and environmental sound are seamlessly combined. They also allow her to rapidly adjust the volume on the earbuds themselves without having to take out her phone.

Jenna occasionally visits the bar in the evenings. She is a big fan of the L.A. Lakers, and whenever they play, she streams the live footage through her phone. Her new earbuds allow her to easily switch to hearing everything around her and streaming the match commentary without having to ever take the earbuds out. She sometimes gets compliments on how stylish the earbuds look on her, and she wouldn’t want to miss out on hearing those either.

docs.title: Aspects
docs.text:
The new product design will be based on that of the AirPods with improvements based on the following requirements. The P1 - P10 is the "code" to indicate the priority of the requirement, from low to high.

  1. Producer Design
  2. 1.1 The product shall be visually easy to distinguish from existing AirPods as well as main competitors Sony WF-1000XM3, Jabra Elite, Amazon Echo Buds, Samsung Galaxy Buds, and Bose SoundSport Free, and Urbanista Stockholm. (P10)
  3. 1.1 The product shall be easy to recognize as an Apple product without needing a logo on its exterior. (P10)

  4. 1.2. The product shall avoid styling elements from our Powerbeats over-ear wireless headphones since those address a different market segment. (P8)

  5. Functionality

    • 2.1 The product shall incorporate one or more optical proximity sensors to detect the user wearing it. (P10)
    • 2.2 The product shall offer a dual microphone in each earbud. (P10)

docs.title: Team Coordination and Accountability
docs.text:
The team will make sure the assignments are submitted before the due date and make sure each team member has ok’d before submitting, by having the project monitor ensure the work is completed 12 hours before the due date. The team will make sure each member has the knowledge and skill needed for each assignment, and will we adjust by having transparent communication, and being open minded on feedback. The team will make sure the feedback given from our design review is distributed and acted on by each team member during our weekly check ins to make sure each member is updated on everything.

Additional questions were asked between the team:

  1. How will the team address missed contributions/assignments/actions? The project monitor will text the person privately.
  2. How will the team hold each other accountable to the expectations of the charter? As a team we can reflect on who did what after each project or assignment in order to figure out responsibility moving forward.
  3. How will the team recognize that a team member is underperforming? Depending on the amount of work designated and quality of work to the member. We will do overall weekly check ins to see if anyone is struggling.
  4. How will the team help an underperforming team member improve? As a team we can offer assistance and help the individual improve their team work and collaboration skills.
  5. What is the agreed upon consequence if an underperforming team member doesn’t improve? We will try to communicate first. If there is no improvement, we will move forward with the pink slip.

docs.title: Conflict Recognition & Resolution
docs.text:
The team handle disagreements during the weekly check ins to discuss any issues and try to solve it as a team. We will make sure everyone feels comfortable expressing their opinion by having constant open dialogue. We will prevent conflicts of interest, or if one person is taking on too many roles by assigning roles/duties as a team for every project.

The steps we decided on to resolve conflicts will be: 1. Ask with an open dialogue about needed support 2. Reminder about assigned duties 3. Team assistance for one assignment 4. Contact the instructor

We decided that a problem that will get an instructor involved is if a team member has to take over another person's responsibility to submit the assignment on time more than once. The current meeting leader or meeting recorder will contact the instructor if a conflict needs to be addressed by them. Overall, the agreed upon process for resolving conflicts is through communication at weekly check ins with all members present.
